summary: Say the counting numbers in order up to 20, with only a slip now and then.
Say which number comes just before or just after another number from 1 to 10.
Count up to 10 things and know the last number said tells how many are in the group.
See how many are in a small group of 1 to 5 straight away, without counting.
Read the written numbers up to 10 and match each one to the amount it stands for.
Compare two groups of up to 10 things and say which has more, which has less, or that they're equal.
Solve small number problems in simple ways, like counting, and tell how they worked it out.
Put small groups together or split them apart, then say how many are in the new group.
Match two groups one to one to show they have the same number of things.
Compare two groups by counting or matching and use words like more, less, fewer and equal.
Compare and group things by length, weight or size, and explain why they go together.
Sort things by two features at once, like big blue and small red, and compare how many in each.
Put familiar things into groups by kind, such as fruits in one group and vegetables in another.
Put things in order by size or length, from smallest to biggest or shortest to longest.
Measure and compare with tools or everyday things, like finding a table is three hands long.
Use time words like before, after, now, later, yesterday and tomorrow the right way.
Name common flat and solid shapes and talk about their parts, like a triangle having three corners.
Put shapes together to make new shapes, and take shapes apart into smaller ones.
Use words like on top of, beside and in front of to say where things are.
Follow simple directions about position, such as stand beside, between or next to something.
Finish a 9 to 12 piece jigsaw puzzle by looking at the picture and the shapes of the pieces.
